title: Molecular Genetics
seo_title: Secondary 4 Biology: Molecular Genetics Worksheets (O-Level 6093 with Answers)
standard_text: Outline the structure of DNA as a double helix of nucleotides with complementary base pairing; describe a gene as a sequence of DNA that codes for a polypeptide and its location on a chromosome; state that the sequence of bases (triplets) determines the order of amino acids; outline how mRNA is made in the nucleus and used at ribosomes to make a protein; describe genetic engineering using restriction enzymes, plasmids and DNA ligase, for example to make human insulin, and discuss its benefits and concerns (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Biology 6093 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Biology worksheets on molecular genetics: DNA structure, base pairing, genes, mRNA, protein synthesis and genetic engineering. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A–T and C–G. Three bases code for one amino acid.
body_html:
How to think about it

DNA is a code for proteins.

  • DNA: two strands of nucleotides in a double helix. A pairs with T, C pairs with G, so %A = %T and %C = %G.
  • A gene is a length of DNA coding for a polypeptide. Each triplet of bases codes for one amino acid.
  • Transcription makes mRNA (with U instead of T) in the nucleus; translation at ribosomes joins amino acids.
  • Genetic engineering: restriction enzyme cuts the gene and plasmid, ligase joins them, bacteria make the protein (insulin).
Example

DNA has 30% A. %G?

T = 30%

G + C = 40%

Answer: 20%

Example

Protein of 120 amino acids. Bases?

120 × 3

Answer: 360

Common mistakes

  • Pairing A with G.
  • Putting thymine in mRNA.
  • Saying one base codes for one amino acid.
  • Mixing up genes and chromosomes.

faq.q: How do you work out base percentages in DNA?
faq.a: A = T and C = G. If A is 30%, then T is 30%, so C + G = 40% and C = G = 20%.

faq.q: How does a gene control the making of a protein?
faq.a: The base sequence of the gene is copied into mRNA in the nucleus. The mRNA goes to a ribosome, where each triplet codes for one amino acid in the polypeptide.

faq.q: How is human insulin made by bacteria?
faq.a: The insulin gene is cut out with a restriction enzyme and joined into a plasmid with DNA ligase. The plasmid is put into bacteria, which are grown in a fermenter and make insulin.

items.q: Why is human insulin from bacteria useful to people with diabetes?
